page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor with 4 physical cores and hyper-threading, this instance allocates dedicated CPU resources. The processor architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which accelerate vector and matrix operations. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks position the n4-highcpu-8 in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1877.0 and a multi-core score of 7215.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 12045.57. Memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 568.81 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 68.85 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks, though its PassMark memory score falls into the weak tier at 1718.22. For specialized tasks, the instance handles static web serving at 11.89 GB/sec and processes Redis SET operations at 8.82 million operations per second. Large language model inference speeds reach 52.37 tokens per second for prompt processing on a medium 7B model, but drop to a weak 7.92 tokens per second for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-highcpu-8 offers a balanced resource density for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it a practical choice for CPU-bound tasks where paying for excess memory would be inefficient. However, the lack of local storage and weak memory performance in specific synthetic benchmarks represent notable tradeoffs. This instance is best suited for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, lightweight text and image processing, and moderate database operations.
